text:
eli: seeing a persistent 99th+ latency spike on kv-heavy long-context workloads on dedicated-gpu-7, looks like KV cache memory grows instead of stabilizing and we hit paging under pressure. repro window: ~30-90s after a long stream starts. heap growth: +420MB in 45s. pprof snapshot attached below in-thread

infra-bot: prod.alert: redispatcher.kv_evictions rate doubled over last 5m on dedicated-gpu-7 :warning:

maya: interesting. did we change the evicter comparator or probation policy recently?

eli: not in config, last change was batching heuristic tweak (continuous batching opt) two days ago. but profiling shows a lot of reinsert churn, entries being evicted then immediately reinserted by hot requests. looks like reuse is failing under bursty allocations. snippet:```text
pprof heap: total 1.8GB
  0.45GB kv_entries (live)
  0.38GB kv_fragments (malloc)
  churn/reinserts: ~1200 ops/s
  avg eviction-to-reuse latency: 18ms
```

sam: can you paste the eviction trace? curious whether LRU markers are flipping or if FIFO bucket rotation is to blame.

eli: pasted an abbreviated trace:```text
evict: id=0x7f34e insert_ts=1716201180 last_access=1716201223 policy=LRU
reinsert: id=0x7f34e by worker=decoder-11 after miss resolution
cache_size before=1.3GB after=1.72GB
page_faults spiked concurrently
```

zhang: I reproduced locally with a synthetic long-stream runner. Repro steps: 1) open 16 concurrent streams, each appending 8k tokens; 2) force batching threshold to 60ms; 3) watch evict/reinsert. I see FIFO runs keep moving older entries to tail but reinserts push them to head causing order inversion.

nora: sounds like a race where reinsert code assumes ownership of entry and moves it to MRU but pagers may mark as evicted concurrently. If reinsert path uses non-atomic list ops we can get inconsistent order and double-counts. Suggestion: add a lightweight per-entry seq counter and CAS on reinsert to ensure we only promote entries we 'own'. Also add metrics for evict->reinsert latency histogram.

maya: good call. also check the eviction watermark hysteresis. If the threshold is too tight under burst, pager will aggressively evict which increases reinsert churn and causes fragmentation. Can we try widening cooldown from 50ms to 200ms as an experiment?

sam: I ran a microbench with both policies. Baseline (LRU, cool=50ms): 99p latency 310ms. LRU + seq-CAS patch + cool=200ms: 99p 140ms. FIFO variant had slightly lower mean but much higher tail when churn present. logs:```text
baseline: tail=310ms, reinserts=1200/s, page-faults=250/s
patched: tail=140ms, reinserts=320/s, page-faults=80/s
```

eli: nice. question on correctness: are there cases where LRU invariants are violated leading to stale cache lookup (i.e., same key present twice or reinserted stale pointer)? I saw one NPE in repro where a stale pointer referenced freed memory.

nora: if we have double-insert without proper tombstoning, we can get stale pointers. Fixes: tombstone on eviction and only reuse slot after epoch increment; or use hazard pointers/pin counts on active reads. Tombstone+seq seems simplest with minimal perf cost.

zhang: added a small patch to tombstone evicted entries and bump epoch, ran the local repro for 30m — no memory growth and tail stable. Will open PR w/ bench.

infra-bot: deploy: canary rollout started for evict-tombstone-seq on dedicated-gpu-7 (3/10 hosts)

eli: rolling canary now. I'll keep an eye on the telemetry (evict/reinsert rates, page faults, 99p). If canary looks good we'll promote. Thanks all for quick triage :thumbsup:

maya: also add a dashboard panel showing reinserts per-second and evict->reuse latency; we didn't have that before and it made root cause harder to spot.

sam: one more note: quantization kernels cause longer KV serialize/deserialize on cold loads, that increases eviction->reinsert window. let's instrument kernel latency buckets per model so we can correlate.

eli: agreed. saving action items: 1) PR for tombstone+seq (zhang), 2) canary rollout monitor (eli), 3) widen eviction cooldown to 200ms in canary (maya), 4) add evict->reinsert hist + kernel latency correlation (sam).

nora: if canary passes, follow-up: upstream evicter refactor to make reinsert atomic by design (saves us from many ad-hoc fixes).

eli: thanks — ping me in thread with the canary metrics.
